messages.subject: measurementInvarianceCat error
parts:
I have a variable group with 3 groups (n1= n2= n3=), a three-factor model with five items in each factor.

I run:

measurementInvarianceCat(model, data = data, group = "group", estimator="WLSMV",ordered=ordered, std.lv = TRUE, strict = T)

And I get:

Error in lav_fit_measures(object = object, fit.measures = fit.measures, : lavaan ERROR: fit measures not available if model did not converge


Although if I run:

#configural
config <- cfa(model, data = data, group = "group", estimator="WLSMV",ordered=ordered, std.lv=T)
fitMeasures(config, c("Df","Chisq", "cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled"))

#weak
model_weak <- cfa(model, data = data, group = "group", estimator="WLSMV",ordered=ordered,
group.equal = c("loadings"), std.lv=T)
fitMeasures(USEI_model_weak, c("Df","Chisq", "cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled"))

#strong
model_strong=cfa(model, data = data, group = "group", estimator="WLSMV",ordered=ordered,
group.equal = c("loadings",
"thresholds"), std.lv=T) 
fitMeasures(USEI_model_strong, c("Df","Chisq", "cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled"))

#strict
model_strict=cfa(model, data = data, group = "group", estimator="WLSMV",ordered=ordered,
group.equal = c("loadings",
"thresholds", "residuals"), std.lv=T) 
fitMeasures(USEI_model_strict, c("Df","Chisq", "cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled"))


#full invariance
model_full=cfa(USEI, data = USEIdf.Areas, group = "AreasCientificas_INV_ENG", estimator="WLSMV",ordered=ordered.usei,
group.equal = c("loadings",
"thresholds", "residuals",
"means"), std.lv=T) 
fitMeasures(USEI_model_full, c("Df","Chisq", "cfi.scaled", "rmsea.scaled"))

I get results without warning (expect the bivariate tables empty cells). Some questions:

1 - with the second approach, I get different results from what I get with the first one (I tested with other grouping variable and I get equal results only for the first model), why?
2 - with the second approach, I get exactly the same results dfs included between the strong and strict invariance models, is there anything wrong in the syntax?
3 - does the second approach compare more than 3 groups? When I run the "summary" function using one of the models (e.g. weak invariance model ) I only see results from the first 2 groups.
4 - which is the function that allows me to obtain SB-delta-chi-square between the fit of two models?

Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvarianceCat error
parts: 1 - with the second approach, I get different results from what I get with the first one (I tested with other grouping variable and I get equal results only for the first model), why?

The semTools function fits different models than you are fitting, using the method recommended by Millsap & Tein (2004).  Unfortunately, their recommended identification method leads to a lot of convergence problems.  Read through this thread for details:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/7sglArLoIno/wBzjM4keDwAJ
2 - with the second approach, I get exactly the same results dfs included between the strong and strict invariance models, is there anything wrong in the syntax?
Again, see the thread I linked to above for details.
3 - does the second approach compare more than 3 groups? When I run the "summary" function using one of the models (e.g. weak invariance model ) I only see results from the first 2 groups.

You can check:

lavInspect(fit, "ngroups")
4 - which is the function that allows me to obtain SB-delta-chi-square between the fit of two models?

?lavTestLRT

Note that neither SB correction (2001 or 2010 -- both are scaled only) is applied in the case of caetgorical data estimated with DWLS.  The Satorra (2000) method (scaled and shifted) is applied with DWLS.
